title: NGC 2420: SDSS DR18 photometry

facility.instrument: 2.5 m Sloan Foundation Telescope, Apache Point Observatory
facility.pipeline: SDSS DR18 imaging (the Star view, PSF magnitudes)

license.statement: SDSS data are in the public domain. SDSS asks that work using them acknowledge the survey and cite the data release (NOTICE).

columns.name: g
columns.description: SDSS g PSF magnitude (psfMag_g), not corrected for extinction

columns.name: r
columns.description: SDSS r PSF magnitude (psfMag_r), not corrected for extinction

masks.rule: SDSS's clean-photometry flag: a star that is saturated, near an edge or deblended badly is dropped
a star fainter than g = 22.5, where SDSS photometry becomes incomplete, is dropped

reductions: Every star within 14.14 arcmin of the adopted center (RA 114.602, Dec +21.575; Cantat-Gaudin et al. 2020, A&A 640, A1 (VizieR J/A+A/640/A1)): a circle of 10 arcmin and an annulus of the same area around it, so the cluster and a field of equal size can be compared.
Of the stars dropped as not clean, 38 are brighter than g = 14.5, where SDSS saturates: the cluster's brightest giants are not in this table.

SDSS's standard photometry has almost nothing at the cluster's center: 3 detections of any kind within 2 arcmin and 15 within 3 (DR18 PhotoObjAll), because its pipeline does not separate stars in so crowded a field (An et al. 2008 remeasured such fields for that reason). The core is missing from this table, not from the sky.
Positions are rounded to 0.00001 degree (0.04 arcsec), magnitudes to 1 mmag and their errors to 0.5 mmag.
The SDSS object ids are left out; the query in the pack's manifest returns them.

queries: SELECT s.ra, s.dec, s.psfMag_g, s.psfMagErr_g, s.psfMag_r, s.psfMagErr_r FROM dbo.fGetNearbyObjEq(114.602,21.575,14.1421) AS nb JOIN Star AS s ON s.objID = nb.objID WHERE s.clean = 1 AND s.psfMag_g < 22.5 ORDER BY s.objID

SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN s.clean = 1 AND s.psfMag_g < 22.5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS kept, SUM(CASE WHEN s.clean = 0 AND s.psfMag_g < 22.5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unclean, SUM(CASE WHEN s.clean = 0 AND s.psfMag_g < 14.5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS uncleanBright, SUM(CASE WHEN s.psfMag_g >= 22.5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS faint FROM dbo.fGetNearbyObjEq(114.602,21.575,14.1421) AS nb JOIN Star AS s ON s.objID = nb.objID
SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN nb.distance < 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS within2, COUNT(*) AS within3 FROM dbo.fGetNearbyObjEq(114.602,21.575,3) AS nb JOIN PhotoObjAll AS s ON s.objID = nb.objID

citations.text: York et al. 2000, AJ 120, 1579 (the Sloan Digital Sky Survey)
An et al. 2008, ApJS 179, 326 (SDSS photometry of crowded cluster fields)

steps: Query the SDSS DR18 Star view for every star within 14.1421 arcmin of the adopted center with clean photometry and g < 22.5, ordered by object id.
Count, in a second query over the same circle, the stars that are not clean or fainter, for the masks.
Encode as table-columns/1: each column a whole number of its step from an offset, int16 where the range fits.

assumptions: PSF magnitudes, as the SDSS pipeline measures them; not corrected for extinction, which a reader applies with a reddening they choose.

validation.check: stars brighter than g = 20 are more than 1.2 times as dense between 3 and 8 arcmin of the center as between 10 and 14.14 arcmin

against.ref: Cantat-Gaudin et al. 2020, A&A 640, A1 (VizieR J/A+A/640/A1)
